summary.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind

details: Foundation models are organized around modality-specific objectives (next-token, next-frame, next-action), so their learned representations are tied to a particular output space rather than to the state of the world.
Goal: a single latent world representation that can be read out for understanding, prediction, and action.

Orca, an encoder-decoder 'world foundation model' whose encoder is trained by Next-State-Prediction: latent world states are abstracted from multimodal signals and transitioned forward/backward under implicit dynamics and explicit conditions.

Two complementary training paradigms realized via learnable query tokens on a VLM backbone: unconscious learning (predict the latent of the next video frame from the current frame, dense self-supervision) and conscious learning (predict the latent of a frame in a language-described adjacent past/future event, plus VQA next-token supervision).

Design principle for validation: after pre-training the encoder is frozen and only lightweight modality-specific readout decoders (text, image, action) are trained, so downstream quality probes the latent itself.
Backbones: Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-4B native VLMs; vision encoder frozen and used as the supervision target for predicted visual latents.
Latent-matching loss = 0.1·MSE + 0.9·cosine; total loss = 0.1·L_obs + 0.5·L_evt + 0.4·L_vqa; 256 learnable queries trained from scratch; state-transition:VQA sampling ≈ 5:1.
10,844 steps on 256 GPUs, AdamW, cosine schedule, ~12.5K video hours consumed (one-tenth of the inventory).
Infrastructure built on FlagScale with FSDP2, chunked cross-entropy, activation recompute, and all-gather prefetching.

Inventory of 125K hours of real-world video (ego-centric interaction, exo-centric manipulation, action-free robot execution, natural dynamics), 160M multi-level event annotations with captions, and 11.5M VQA samples.
No action labels are used during pre-training.
Language: reuse the backbone LM head, no new module.
Vision: MLP adaptor (latent 64x2560 -> SD3.5 conditioning) plus LoRA on a frozen Stable Diffusion 3.5 MMDiT/VAE; 768x768 targets, 200K steps.

Action: DiT-based Action Expert (8 blocks, flow-matching) trained from scratch, conditioned on the query latent, proprioception, and noisy actions; action horizon 30; 200 real-robot trajectories per task, 20K steps.

Text: MVBench, TemporalBench, 3DSRBench, SWITCH (zero-shot), versus world models (V-JEPA 2.1, Emu3, Emu3.5) and VLMs (Qwen3.5, Gemma 4, DeepSeek-VL2, MiniCPM-V-4.6, SmolVLM2); plus a cross-benchmark re-grouping into state transition, commonsense, spatial, dynamic-motion dimensions.

Image: newly constructed PRICE-V0.1 real-world instruction-conditioned image-prediction benchmark (AgiBot-World, HomeInteract, PE-Video, PSI-Ego), scored 1-5 by Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT 5.4, Doubao-Seed-2.0-Pro and Gemma 4-31B; baselines OmniGen2, FLUX.1-Kontext, FLUX.2 [klein].

Action: five dual-arm wheeled-robot tasks under environment-OOD and object-OOD settings; rule-based key-stage scores plus PRM-as-a-Judge trajectory diagnostics; baselines V-JEPA 2.1 and Qwen3.5 with the identical Action Expert, and pi_0.5 pre-trained on large-scale robot data.
Ablation over the three loss terms (L_obs, L_evt, L_vqa).

key_findings.finding: With the backbone frozen, downstream readout quality in all three modalities improves monotonically as pre-training data and model size grow, indicating a stronger world latent yields stronger readouts.
key_findings.evidence: Total pre-training loss decreases steadily with video hours and is lower for 4B than 0.8B without early convergence; probing intermediate checkpoints of Orca-0.8B and Orca-4B shows rising averages on text benchmarks, PRICE-V0.1, and five real-robot OOD tasks.

key_findings.finding: Action generation benefits from purely video-based state-transition pre-training despite no action labels ever being seen, closing the gap with a robot-data-pretrained VLA.
key_findings.evidence: With identical from-scratch Action Experts on 200 trajectories/task, Orca-4B reaches 32.4 overall rule-based score versus Qwen3.5 10.5 (0% success) and V-JEPA 2.1 17.0, exceeding pi_0.5's 29.4 overall and 27.6 vs 36.6 on environment OOD; Orca also has the highest drawdown recovery ratio (30.3 vs 26.7).

key_findings.finding: The learned latent transfers to text and image readouts, beating same-size specialist models and much larger world models.
key_findings.evidence: Text average 51.8 for Orca-4B versus 46.7 for Qwen3.5-4B, 40.8 for Gemma 4-4B, and 29.8-30.4 for Emu3.5-34B/Emu3-8B; on PRICE-V0.1 Orca (4B+2B) scores 59.8+-10.9 average across four judges versus FLUX.2 [klein] 56.1+-18.1, FLUX.1-Kontext 40.9, OmniGen2 39.6.

key_findings.finding: The three pre-training objectives play distinct, complementary roles: observation-only transition drives action readout while event-conditioned transition drives image readout.
key_findings.evidence: Ablation: dropping L_obs lowers action score from 32.4 to 23.0; dropping L_evt (obs+vqa only) removes image readout capability while action stays high at 32.6; the full combination gives the best balance (48.0 average across the three readouts).
